newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Rubber prices stable at Colombo auction.
newsitem.headline: Rubber prices stable at Colombo auction.

text.p: Crepe prices were stable at Thursday's Colombo auction, but brokers warned of falling quantities in future auctions if present rains continued.
"The market was strong today. All grades were in demand," said Upali Bandaranayake of brokers Forbes and Walker.
"But the market is unable to get desired quantites because of rain. If the rains continue, quantities will really come down," he said.
On Thursday, the auction offered 212.6 tonnes of latex, 13.5 tonnes of sheet and 31 tonnes of scrap.

The average price for the purest grade, best latex one-x, rose to 73.85 rupees ($1.30) per kg from 73.75 on Tuesday when the auction was last held. Number one was unchanged at 72.50. RSS 1 was slightly down at 63.60 from Tuesday's 64 rupees.
A leading exporter of the commodity said buyers had adopted a wait-and-see attitude as unusually heavy rains lashed growing areas, reducing rubber quantities.

"People still want a lot of rubber but they are unsure if the quantities can be sourced in this market," he said. Rain brings production to a virtual standstill and affects the quality of whatever is tapped, brokers said. ($1=56.58 rupees)
